title: Mini-horizon anchor: collapsed legend summaries + ARIA cue profiles for high-density time-series
creator: Ana Park
description:
Problem: High-density time-series embeddings in dashboards cause very long legend DOM lists and noisy screen reader output. We need a compact, collapsible legend anchor (mini-horizon) that surfaces a short machine-friendly summary for SRs and a single-line visual token for dense views. This ticket defines the design tokens, keyboard/voice interactions, and the accessibility cue profiles that engineering will implement, plus performance constraints to keep reflows under target budgets.

Goal: Deliver a reusable legend component variant (mini-horizon) and an ARIA announcement profile (aria-cue) that: 1) reduces DOM nodes for large series sets, 2) provides a concise SR-friendly summary of visible series and highlights, 3) preserves keyboard navigation and contextual focus, and 4) fits into the design system token model so teams can opt into compact rendering without custom CSS hacks.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec and token mapping committed to the component library design tokens page
Figma mockups for collapsed/expanded states and keyboard focus states reviewed and approved
ARIA cue profiles documented with examples and expected SR output strings for common states
Performance budget: legend mount/update for 200 series < 40ms on a mid-range laptop (measured in Lighthouse 3rd party environment)
Engineering acceptance: prototype PR exists with feature flag `miniHorizon=true` and unit tests for announced summaries
design_notes: Introduce two new tokens: token.legend.horizon-height (default 28px) and token.legend.horizon-density-threshold (default 12 series) to switch to mini-horizon mode.
Visual: mini-horizon shows up to 6 condensed color swatches + a trailing counter (+34) when density > threshold; expanded tray reveals full list.
Interaction: single Tab lands on collapsed anchor; Space/Enter expands to tray; Arrow keys move inside tray; Escape collapses and returns focus to anchor.
Screen reader profile: use aria-live polite for small updates; on expand, announce `n series visible, x highlighted` using concise tokens; avoid reading all series names by default.
Fallbacks: on audio-only or assistive devices with high verbosity preference, provide a verbose mode controllable via settings (observer preference).
dev_notes: Recommend implementing legend items as virtualized list rows to avoid rendering all DOM nodes when density is high.
Provide a compact render path that uses a canvas-based color band for the condensed swatch strip; exposes hit targets for keyboard and mouse via an accessible overlay.
Expose hooks: onMiniHorizonToggle, onRequestAnnounce(summaryString) for Console telemetry and test harness to validate SR output.
Quantify token mapping in a design tokens JSON and include migration notes for existing CSS vars.
Perf tests: create a synthetic dashboard story with 2000 points across 300 series. Capture CPU/paint timings and optimize reflows — aim to batch style updates and avoid layout thrash.
qa_checks: VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Win10) tests: collapsed anchor announces count and toggles correctly
Keyboard only: verify tab stops, expand/collapse via Enter/Space, arrow navigation inside tray, Escape collapse behavior
High-contrast and large text modes: condensed swatches remain distinguishable and meet 3:1 contrast where possible
Performance: run storybook scenario and verify legend mount/update < 40ms for 200 series on lab machine (specs linked in attachments)
Regression: ensure existing compact legend CSS variables remain backward compatible
